_readme: The registry for the ajit-segment-bots blueprint. The diagram is drawn from
this file and nothing else. Nothing here is invented: categories and features
come from the user, and each carries the origin it came from.
EVERY PART IS A TRANSISTOR. docs/transistor-rule.md is the shape of a part and
it decides how every feature is built. Six rules, all checked by
dashboard/check_contracts.py and refused by the git pre-commit hook:
T-1  every feature is the same shape -- one template, no exemptions
T-2  control path separate from data path -- only the governor switches parts
T-3  off means genuinely off -- an off part releases its CPU and RAM
T-4  a part knows nothing about the circuit -- it names data, never parts
T-5  states are explicit and countable, drawn from state_vocabulary
T-6  grow by adding parts, never by making a part cleverer
R-01 in docs/contracts.md keeps the data plane whole: edges are computed from
consumes/produces, so a part swaps out cleanly and none can wire itself in.
categories[]       the foundation blocks. Every feature belongs to exactly one.
id, name, summary, origin ('user' | 'proposed'), approved
state_vocabulary[] the closed set of states a part may be in. Extending it is a
deliberate decision, never a smuggled flag (T-5).
data_types[]       id, name, description -- what actually moves between parts
features[]         id, name, role, category, consumes[], produces[], switchable,
off_releases_resources, states[], replaces?
features[] is empty until the user describes them. data_types[] is empty
until the flow between categories is declared. Neither is guessed.

categories.name: Paper trading on live data
categories.summary: Trading runs on live market data, with a switch between real money and paper money.

categories.name: Universal opportunity scanner
categories.summary: Constantly monitors every symbol in the segment and picks when one should enter trading. It holds no built-in rules: what counts as an opportunity arrives as instructions from the hypothesis feature. An opportunity can be anything -- a sudden price jump implying a minor pullback, for instance -- and the response depends on the segment. Lives inside the segment bot. Does not know whether the money is paper or live.

categories.name: Segment bot (bull, bear, profit tailgating)
categories.summary: The container. Inside it: the universal opportunity scanner, the AI brain, and three bots -- bull, bear and profit tailgating. The bots issue opinions; the brain turns three opinions into one intent.

categories.name: Intelligence
categories.summary: A peer block, side by side with the AI brain and hypothesis rather than inside either. Named by the user; its one-line job is not yet given, so it has no flow.

categories.name: Learning loop
categories.summary: Keeps the score the bots learn from: each bot's right and wrong calls, which features actually preceded profit, and whether a bot has earned its way out of exploration.

categories.name: Hypothesis
categories.summary: Takes what closed trades taught and turns it into opportunity instructions for the scanner. Explicitly includes thinking about how the information in a losing trade becomes an opening profit trade. Further internals not yet described.

categories.name: Knowledge
categories.summary: Three memory tiers that disagree with each other on purpose: semantic facts per symbol upserted under closed-set keys, episodic closed trades appended immutably and keyed on the condition observed, and a procedural playbook that is never searched and always injected. Shape proposed from research, not given by the user.

categories.name: Prediction
categories.summary: Predicts what the market does next, from candles alone. Built on Kronos, the open-source foundation model for K-line sequences: a tokenizer quantises OHLCV into hierarchical discrete tokens, an autoregressive transformer continues the sequence. Both halves are finetuned on the assets actually traded here.

categories.name: Online research
categories.summary: Decodes the portfolios of famous or high-profit crypto traders to copy their strategy or step up beyond it. Reads through front doors only -- venue leaderboard APIs and public chain explorers -- because the data that matters is published, and typed data survives a redesign where scraped HTML does not.

categories.name: LLM services
categories.summary: Infrastructure first: it makes model calls and returns answers, holds no opinion about trading and decides nothing, so there is one place to swap models, cap cost and cache. A reasoning role of its own is a planned extension, not a gap.
categories.planned_extension: Becomes a thinker in its own right once the rest is running — reasoning about the market rather than only answering other blocks' questions.

categories.name: Hardware resource governor
categories.summary: An AI agent that scans the hardware and keeps every other part working without queueing: allocating CPU and RAM, swapping parts fast, turning off a part that is hogging the machine and turning on the part that needs it. This is why R-02 exists -- it cannot turn off a part that has no off switch.

categories.name: Market data feed
categories.summary: Exchange connectivity, reconnects, gap detection and symbol normalisation across venues. The substrate the scanner, prediction and paper-fill pricing all read from.

categories.name: Risk and capital allocation
categories.summary: Position size, leverage, exposure caps, drawdown limits and the kill switch. The bots decide direction; this decides how much, and when to refuse.

categories.name: Ledger and audit trail
categories.summary: Every scan, decision, order, fill and price recorded. What the learning loop learns from, and what hypothesis and prediction are scored against.

categories.name: Portfolio and position state
categories.summary: What is held right now, per segment, reconciled against the exchange. The scanner needs to know what is already open before calling a new entry.

categories.name: Observability
categories.summary: Health and state of every part, feeding the dashboard. As a category it forces each part to emit its own state rather than have it inferred later.

categories.name: Execution and venue adapter
categories.summary: Placing orders for real: partial fills, rejects, retries, rate limits. The user chose it standing on its own rather than nested inside paper/live trading.

categories.name: AI brain
categories.summary: Arbitrates. Each of the three bots emits a direction with conviction; the brain weighs them and issues the single trade intent that leaves the segment bot. This is why it sits inside the segment bot rather than beside it.

categories.name: Closed trade decoding
categories.summary: Decodes finished trades — winners and losers both — into instructions for the hypothesis feature. Portfolio state signals that a position closed; the ledger supplies that trade's full history, every scan, intent, sizing and fill that led to it. The loser is not discarded: its information is what hypothesis works on.

categories.name: Skills
categories.summary: Reads books, research papers, community chats and anything else, and converts each into a skill the brains load on demand. Distilled into structure -- frameworks, decision rules, anti-patterns -- never a summary. Only the section a question needs is loaded, so the library can be large without costing anything until it is used.

data_types.name: market data
data_types.description: Live prices, trades and book for every symbol, normalised across venues.

data_types.name: entry candidate
data_types.description: A symbol and the moment it should enter trading. Carries nothing about paper or live.

data_types.name: trade intent
data_types.description: A direction and conviction for a candidate, from the bull, bear and profit-tailgating bots.

data_types.name: sized order
data_types.description: A trade intent with size, leverage and stops applied — or a refusal, which is also an answer.

data_types.name: order request
data_types.description: An order addressed to a destination, after the paper/live switch has chosen one.

data_types.name: fill
data_types.description: What actually executed, at what price, including partials and rejects.

data_types.name: position
data_types.description: What is held right now, per segment, reconciled against the venue.

data_types.name: journal entry
data_types.description: An immutable record of something that happened, with the time it happened.

data_types.name: research finding
data_types.description: A decoded strategy or portfolio from a public high-profit trader.

data_types.name: part health
data_types.description: A part's own state and health, emitted by the part rather than inferred about it.

data_types.name: opportunity instruction
data_types.description: What the scanner should watch for and what it implies. The user's words: opportunities are instructions or feeds derived from the hypothesis feature, not rules built into the scanner.

data_types.name: closed trade
data_types.description: A finished trade with its outcome, profit or loss, and everything that led to it.

data_types.name: decoded trade instruction
data_types.description: What a closed trade taught, drawn from winners and losers alike, expressed as an instruction for the hypothesis feature to work on.

data_types.name: LLM request
data_types.description: A question a block asks a language model. The asking block names this data type, never the LLM block.

data_types.name: LLM response
data_types.description: The model's answer, returned to whichever block asked.

data_types.name: K-line window
data_types.description: A fixed-length run of OHLCV candles, the shape the Kronos tokenizer expects. Bounded by the model's context limit.

data_types.name: price forecast
data_types.description: Predicted candles for the periods ahead, with the model version that produced them.

data_types.name: forecast accuracy
data_types.description: How a past forecast actually scored against what the market did. A forecast nobody scores is an assertion.

data_types.name: finetuned model
data_types.description: Kronos weights adapted to the assets actually traded here, tokenizer included.

data_types.name: model choice
data_types.description: Which Kronos size to run: mini, small or base.

data_types.name: volatility feature set
data_types.description: The ten realised- and implied-volatility features from the reel, computed for one symbol.

data_types.name: volatility forecast
data_types.description: Forward realised volatility estimated from the feature set. Distinct from a price forecast: it says how much, not which way.

data_types.name: implied volatility surface
data_types.description: ATM implied vol, the 30-60 term slope and the 25-delta put skew. Only exists where an options venue does.

data_types.name: market regime
data_types.description: Trending, mean-reverting, or mixed, from a Hurst proxy. Mixed is a real answer meaning stand down.

data_types.name: trade episode
data_types.description: A closed trade keyed on the market condition that was observed, never on the outcome. Immutable.

data_types.name: recalled episode
data_types.description: Past episodes matching a condition seen now.

data_types.name: semantic fact
data_types.description: A durable fact about one symbol, filed under a closed-set key so a contradiction overwrites by construction.

data_types.name: playbook rule
data_types.description: An always-injected, never-searched, capped rule. Behaviour only, never diagnosis.

data_types.name: expectancy breakdown
data_types.description: Expected value split into separately measurable factors, so the weakest one is visible rather than the total merely being poor.

data_types.name: ablation scorecard
data_types.description: What measurably broke when each part was switched off, one row per part.

data_types.name: source document
data_types.description: A source pulled into text, whatever form it arrived in: book, paper, chat log, page.

data_types.name: skill
data_types.description: A source distilled into structure -- frameworks, decision rules, anti-patterns -- with the trigger that says when it applies. Never a summary.

data_types.name: available skill
data_types.description: An indexed skill, findable by what it is for rather than by its title.

data_types.name: loaded skill section
data_types.description: Only the part of a skill the current question needs. This is what lets the library grow without a token cost.

data_types.name: skill usefulness
data_types.description: Whether loading a skill changed the outcome. A skill nobody scores is an assertion.

data_types.name: tracked trader
data_types.description: A high-performing trader worth following, with the venue or wallet that identifies them.

data_types.name: external position
data_types.description: What a tracked trader currently holds, from public explorers or venue leaderboards.

data_types.name: strategy gap
data_types.description: What a decoded strategy does that this bot does not. The 'step up beyond it' half of C-09.

data_types.name: directional opinion
data_types.description: One bot's direction plus conviction on a candidate. An opinion, never an order.

data_types.name: bot scorecard
data_types.description: A bot's own record of right calls against wrong ones. What it learns from.

data_types.name: bot maturity
data_types.description: Whether a bot has graduated out of exploration on its own measured edge.

data_types.name: feature reliability
data_types.description: Which features preceded profitable trades rather than losing ones.

data_types.name: stop adjustment
data_types.description: A protective stop moved up as a position gains, so a pullback keeps some profit rather than giving it all back.

features.name: K-line window builder
features.role: shape live market data into the fixed candlestick window the model expects

features.name: Kronos forecaster
features.role: run the Kronos model over a candlestick window to produce a price forecast

features.name: Kronos finetuner
features.role: adapt the Kronos tokenizer plus predictor to the assets actually traded here

features.name: Forecast scorer
features.role: score each past forecast against what the market actually did

features.name: Kronos size selector
features.role: choose which Kronos model size to run based on measured forecast accuracy

features.name: Implied volatility reader
features.role: read the option surface into implied volatilities at the strikes that matter
features.note: Switched off in spot and futures, which have no option surface. This is what R-02's switch is for: the part exists in every segment and only conducts where it can.

features.name: Volatility feature builder
features.role: compute the realised-volatility feature set from a candlestick window
features.note: RV 1d/5d/22d, downside semivariance over negative returns only, jump variance as max(RV-BV,0), vol-of-vol, ATM IV, 30-60 term slope, 25-delta put skew, market RV.

features.name: Realised volatility regressor
features.role: estimate forward realised volatility from the feature set
features.note: The ten-beta linear model recovered from the reel's final frame.

features.name: Regime classifier
features.role: classify the current regime with a Hurst proxy
features.note: Below 0.5 mean-reverting, above 0.5 trending, and mixed is a real answer. This is the detector the mean-reversion sheet needed but never named.

features.name: Mean reversion detector
features.role: flag a symbol whose price has deviated far enough from its mean
features.note: Z-score entry above 2, exit below 0.5. Stands down when the regime classifier says trending.

features.name: Volatility gap detector
features.role: flag a symbol where forecast volatility disagrees with the option market

features.name: Semantic fact store
features.role: hold durable per-symbol facts under a closed-set key
features.note: Closed-set keys so a contradicting fact lands on the same key by construction and overwrites.

features.name: Episodic trade store
features.role: keep every closed trade as an immutable episode keyed on the condition observed
features.note: Append-only, written on close. Embed the condition, never the outcome.

features.name: Procedural playbook
features.role: hold the capped always-injected rule set that never gets searched
features.note: Never searched, so it never pollutes recall. A fixed cost every scan, which is why it is capped and holds behaviour rather than diagnosis.

features.name: Trade episode encoder
features.role: encode each closed trade keyed on the market condition that was observed
features.note: Key on what was seen, never on what happened. 'Lost 2% on a long' retrieves nothing ever again.

features.name: Lesson extractor
features.role: turn a trade episode into an instruction the hypothesis feature can work on

features.name: Expectancy decomposer
features.role: decompose expected value into separately measurable factors
features.note: The Drake pattern: a chain of separately estimable factors, so the weakest one is visible rather than the total merely being poor.

features.name: Instruction writer
features.role: write the opportunity instruction the scanner will watch for

features.name: Venue candle reader
features.role: read live candles from every venue through one unified interface
features.note: Built on CCXT.

features.name: Venue order router
features.role: place each order on its venue through one unified interface
features.note: Built on CCXT.

features.name: Ablation harness
features.role: measure what breaks when each part is switched off
features.note: Proves R-02 and T-3 rather than asserting them. It measures only: the governor does the switching, because T-2 forbids a feature reaching into the control plane.

features.name: Source ingester
features.role: pull a source into text whatever form it arrived in
features.note: Books, papers, community chats, pages. The form is the ingester's problem, never the distiller's.

features.name: Skill distiller
features.role: distil a source document into a skill with its trigger described
features.note: Structure, not a summary: frameworks, decision rules, anti-patterns, per-section files. A summary is what makes an agent hallucinate confidently.

features.name: Skill index
features.role: hold every skill so one can be found by what it is for
features.note: Found by trigger rather than by title, the same reason episodes embed the condition rather than the outcome.

features.name: Skill loader
features.role: load only the section of a skill that the current question needs
features.note: THE mechanism. Procedural playbook rules are capped because they are always injected; a skill escapes that cap by being loaded only when relevant. The two are complementary, not competing.

features.name: Skill scorer
features.role: score whether a loaded skill changed the outcome
features.note: Lets a skill that never changes anything be retired instead of accumulating.

features.name: Leaderboard reader
features.role: read the public copy-trading leaderboards each venue publishes
features.note: Binance and Bybit publish these with official APIs. A front door, so no bot-detection evasion is needed or wanted.

features.name: On-chain position reader
features.role: read a tracked trader's on-chain positions from public explorers
features.note: Etherscan, Dune, DeBank, Arkham. Typed data that survives a redesign, unlike scraped HTML.

features.name: Strategy decoder
features.role: infer the strategy behind a tracked trader's position history
features.note: The 'decode' half of the user's words. Position history over time, not a single snapshot.

features.name: Edge comparator
features.role: compare a decoded strategy against what this bot already does
features.note: The 'or step up into us' half. Copying is the floor; the gap is where the value is.

features.name: Bull bot
features.role: issue a long-side opinion on an entry candidate
features.note: Learns from its own right and wrong calls with its own features. In spot it is the same template as the bear with the direction configured; in futures and options it is a separate design, because funding is paid rather than received, liquidation is asymmetric, and a short can lose more than it stakes.

features.name: Bear bot
features.role: issue a short-side opinion on an entry candidate
features.note: Same template as the bull in spot, its own design in futures and options. Learns from its own scorecard.

features.name: Profit tailgater
features.role: take a position in something already proven to be working
features.note: Never originates cold. Rides a position already in profit, or follows a high-profit trader that C-09 decoded. Profit protection and scorekeeping were split out of it: see profit-lock and the learning-loop parts.

features.name: Opinion arbiter
features.role: weigh the bots' opinions into one trade intent
features.note: Why the brain sits inside the segment bot. Three opinions in, one intent out. Opposing positions on one symbol are allowed while a bot is still in exploration, and after it graduates only when the regime reads mixed.

features.name: Profit lock
features.role: raise the stop as an open position gains so a pullback keeps some profit
features.note: Lives in risk, not in a bot, deliberately. It defends every open position whoever opened it -- if it sat inside the tailgater then a bull-opened trade would lose protection the moment that bot was switched off, and R-02 says every part can be switched off.

features.name: Bot scorekeeper
features.role: keep each bot's record of right calls against wrong ones
features.note: Pairs each opinion with what the trade actually did. This is what the bots learn from.

features.name: Feature reliability scorer
features.role: score which features preceded profitable trades rather than losing ones
features.note: The user's scorekeeping idea, moved out of the tailgater: it runs after trades close, not during them.

features.name: Edge graduation gate
features.role: graduate a bot out of exploration when its own numbers clear the bar
features.note: Bull and bear graduate separately, per segment, on measured edge rather than on a trade count or a date.

control_plane.note: T-2 — the gate is a third terminal. Only this part switches other parts, and it does so outside the data plane. No feature ever switches another.

segments.note: Every segment is a bot with all of this inside it. The user's words. The same structure is instantiated per segment, and the directional response to an opportunity depends on which segment is reacting -- a put in options is a short in futures.

scope_decision.note: Each segment gets its own of every block. Three risk allocators, three portfolios, three ledgers, three feeds, three hypothesis features. Complete isolation: a fault in one segment cannot reach another, and each segment learns only from itself.
scope_decision.flagged: CONFIRMED by the user 2026-08-20: the hardware resource governor and observability stay global. One machine means one governor -- three of them, each blind to the other two, would compete for the same RAM and recreate the queueing C-11 exists to prevent. One board, one place to look.
scope_decision.edges: The 19 edges were accepted provisionally on 2026-08-20, with the user's words: decide them again when the design is locked and implementation starts. flow_origin reads agreed-provisional, never agreed.

thinking_shape.note: Intelligence, knowledge, prediction, learning loop, hypothesis and the AI brain are peers, side by side. The AI brain is not a container. Each is a block like any other, connected by data.
thinking_shape.still_needed: A one-line job for intelligence, knowledge, prediction and learning loop. Until then they carry no flow rather than an invented one.

upstream_dependencies.name: Kronos
upstream_dependencies.verified: 2026-08-20 via gh, not from the social post
upstream_dependencies.note: Decoder-only foundation model family for K-line sequences from Tsinghua, accepted to AAAI 2026. Model zoo: Kronos-mini 4.1M params context 2048, Kronos-small 24.7M context 512, Kronos-base 102.3M context 512. Kronos-large 499.2M is NOT open-source. Finetuning scripts released 2025-08-17.

upstream_dependencies.name: CCXT
upstream_dependencies.note: One unified API over 100+ exchanges: OHLCV, order placement, balances. Two foundation blocks from one dependency.

upstream_dependencies.name: Freqtrade
upstream_dependencies.note: A complete crypto bot: strategy framework, backtesting, paper trading before real money, live automation. C-01's whole shape already solved.

upstream_dependencies.name: NautilusTrader
upstream_dependencies.note: Event-driven engine built for correctness under load. The reference for structuring an engine meant to be trusted rather than demonstrated.

upstream_dependencies.name: TradingAgents
upstream_dependencies.note: Splits a trading brain into news, market, sentiment, strategy and execution agents. The largest project in the set by a wide margin.

upstream_dependencies.name: Hummingbot
upstream_dependencies.note: Decomposes into core engine, arbitrage scanner, risk manager, strategy executor. An independent team arriving at nearly our block boundaries.

upstream_dependencies.name: FinRL
upstream_dependencies.note: Load data, build environment, train agent, backtest, evaluate, deploy. The closest worked learning loop in the set.

upstream_dependencies.name: VectorBT
upstream_dependencies.note: Vectorised backtesting, built for sweeping thousands of parameter sets. Serves no declared block: this project has no backtesting category yet.

upstream_dependencies.name: Backtrader
upstream_dependencies.note: Not pushed since 2024-08-19 while everything beside it shipped this month. Rejected on staleness, never on licence.

upstream_dependencies.name: Polymarket CLOB client
upstream_dependencies.note: Prediction markets. Only relevant if they enter scope, which they have not.

upstream_dependencies.name: book-to-skill
upstream_dependencies.verified: 2026-08-20 via gh — the post said 16.3k stars, the repo has 23,262
upstream_dependencies.note: Distils a source into a skill of frameworks, decision rules and anti-patterns with per-chapter files, loaded on demand. Emits the open Agent Skills SKILL.md format, which Claude Code, Copilot CLI and Amp all read.

_dependency_note: Licence is recorded as a fact, not a constraint — see D-003: this is a personal project that is not distributed, so GPL and LGPL obligations do not attach. Ranked on merit. 'candidate dependency' means considered for use; 'architecture reference' means read rather than imported.

opposing_positions.exploration: While a bot is still in exploration, bull and bear may both open on the same symbol. It is a live test of which one is right on this kind of setup, and the paired outcome is what the scorekeeper learns from.
opposing_positions.mature: Once a bot graduates on measured edge, opposing positions are allowed only when the regime classifier reads mixed -- a deliberate straddle when there is no trend to take a side on.
opposing_positions.gate: Measured edge, per bot, per segment. Bull and bear graduate separately.
opposing_positions.cost: Two legs means two sets of fees and, in futures, funding on both sides. In a chop both can lose. That is the price of the exploration phase and it is why the phase ends on evidence.
